_comment: REVIEWED CONTRACT for what a compiled rule must carry. ASTRA, PR #24 round 1:
a derivation cannot be the completeness authority. A variable-name heuristic
missed three real matcher reads, and an unrelated dict named `p` plus a module
with PATTERNS in a COMMENT each produced a false kill on a correct artefact.
Dictionary spelling is not evidence of access to a pattern dictionary.
So the authority is this file, and the gate FAILS CLOSED on any source key it
does not classify: a new pattern field cannot ship until someone puts it here
as consulted or as metadata. Derivation still runs and is reported as
DIAGNOSTIC evidence beside it, never as the verdict.
`where` is the lowering. `record` means the compiler must emit the same key on
the compiled record with an equal value. `regex[].anchors` and `regex[].span`
are the measured lowering of the anchored lane: EVERY compiled regex entry of
an anchored rule carries the same anchor set and span (7 rules, 13 entries,
measured on v0.5.9). Regex SEMANTICS stay with the behavioural parity gates;
this file is about fields surviving compilation, not about what they match.

keywords.reason: measured on v0.5.9, 1554/1554 exact: the compiler emits the source's keywords minus SunglassesEngine.KEYWORD_DENYLIST, order preserved -- the same FP-guard strip the engine applies at index-build time (engine.py:468). The denylist is READ FROM THE TAGGED SOURCE, never listed here, so a change to it cannot silently pass this gate.

negation_immune.reason: measured on v0.5.9: 1548 rules omit it and the compiler emits false

regex.reason: the compiler transforms sources and adds guards/requires; entry COUNT is checked here and semantics are the parity gates' job

metadata._comment: Consulted by nothing. The compiler MAY drop these -- `mechanism` is dropped on the one rule that carries it. If it emits one it must EQUAL the source, and it may never invent one the source does not carry.
